changesets.summary: Throw the address-scoped error for non-base58 address characters
changesets.details: `assertIsAddress` validated string length and decoded byte count with dedicated `SolanaErrorCode`s, but a string in range whose characters fall outside the base58 alphabet leaked the codec's own error instead. That input now throws `SolanaErrorCode.addressesInvalidBase58EncodedAddress` with the `putativeAddress` context and the codec failure as its cause, matching the upstream `@solana/kit` error contract. `isAddress` still returns false for the same input.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/address-lookup-table` `js@v0.16.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.16.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Validate Anchor IDL discriminators
changesets.details: Reject missing, empty, non-integer, and out-of-range instruction, account, and event discriminators during IDL parsing. Preserve valid custom lengths and make parsed discriminator bytes immutable. Prevent empty discriminators from matching instruction, account, or event payloads, including when IDL entries are constructed manually.

changesets.summary: Bound fixed-array lengths from runtime schemas
changesets.details:
Anchor IDL type parsing rejects negative, fractional, non-finite, and excessive fixed-array lengths. The upper bound is one million items, shared with array decoders through the new `defaultMaxArrayItems` constant.

Fixed-array decoders now enforce `maxItems` during construction, before byte-size calculations or element reads. This prevents hostile schema lengths from expanding zero-byte elements into unbounded lists. Callers can still choose a different decoder limit with `maxItems`; valid empty arrays and zero-byte elements remain supported.

changesets.summary: Require Anchor IDL names and error codes, and attribute encode failures
changesets.details:
`parseAnchorIdl` silently turned an IDL instruction, error, or defined type with a missing name into the empty string — every such node then collided under the `''` key in the instruction, error, and type maps — and an error entry without a numeric `code` became code zero, silently mis-keying program error decoding. Both now throw `ArgumentError` naming the offending entry.

`AnchorCoder`'s encode helpers no longer drop the field context they are given: a value that fails to encode inside an instruction argument or account field now surfaces as an `ArgumentError` naming that field instead of a bare codec error.

changesets.summary: Reject cyclic Anchor IDL type dependencies
changesets.details: Reject cyclic Anchor IDL type dependencies with an `ArgumentError` during codec construction instead of exhausting the call stack. Apply the check to direct codec requests, instructions, accounts, and events while preserving repeated acyclic references.

changesets.summary: Bound BigInt materialization from plain integer literals
changesets.details: `parseJsonWithBigInts` capped positive-exponent expansion at 10,000 but accepted a plain integer literal of any length, so a hostile RPC response containing a multi-megabyte integer forced a same-sized `BigInt` allocation for a cost far cheaper for the sender than for this process. Integer literals are now rejected when they would materialize more than 10,001 digits — the same ceiling the exponent cap already permits — on both the plain and the mantissa-plus-exponent paths. No value the exponent path accepted before changes.

changesets.summary: Validate blockhash format before it reaches the wire
changesets.details: The wire format stores a blockhash lifetime token as a fixed 32-byte value, but nothing validated the constraint's string: a blockhash whose base58 decoding was not exactly 32 bytes — for example one served by a compromised RPC — was silently truncated or zero-extended by the fixed-size encoder, producing a signed transaction whose lifetime token differs from the string shown to the caller. `setTransactionMessageLifetimeUsingBlockhash` now rejects such values with the new `SolanaErrorCode.transactionInvalidBlockhashFormat` (port-only code `5663043`), the blockhash counterpart of the existing `transactionInvalidNonceFormat` check.

changesets.summary: Verify browser wallet signing results
changesets.details: Reject unverified browser wallet signing results. Check result counts, verify Ed25519 signatures, bind signed transactions and messages to their requests, validate every supplied sign-in challenge field and authorized account, and preserve offchain content and required signers. Copy request bytes before passing them to JavaScript so wallet providers cannot mutate the original request.

changesets.summary: Reject malformed Helius checkout responses instead of silently defaulting them
changesets.details:
The hosted-checkout response models (`CheckoutInitializeResponse`, `CheckoutPreviewResponse`, `CheckoutStatusResponse`) parsed with `?? ''` / `?? 0` / `?? false` fallbacks on every field, so a malformed renewal response could tell a user to pay zero cents to an empty wallet through a payment link that looked real. All three models now parse with the package's `JsonReader` require-accessors and throw `FormatException` naming the missing key, matching the strict parsing the developer-portal API clients already use. `pollCheckoutCompletion`'s documented synthetic pending/expired statuses are unchanged; only genuinely malformed HTTP responses now fail.

`fetchTipFloor75th` still returns null for transient endpoint failures but no longer swallows `ArgumentError` and `TypeError`: a bad endpoint argument now surfaces as a programming error instead of the conservative null tip.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/compute-budget` `js@v0.20.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.20.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Reject DAS responses with missing proof and compression fields
changesets.details: `HeliusDasClient` silently defaulted missing DAS fields — a proof without `node_index` decoded as index zero, a missing `tree_id` as an empty tree address, a missing `leaf_id` as nonce zero — and those values flow directly into the leaf hash, nonce, and index of Bubblegum transfer and mint instructions, producing plausible on-chain garbage. The asset and proof parsers now throw `FormatException` naming the missing field for `id`, `ownership.owner`, `ownership.frozen`, every core `compression` field (`compressed`, `data_hash`, `creator_hash`, `asset_hash`, `tree`, `seq`, `leaf_id`), every `getAssetProof` field (`root`, `proof`, `node_index`, `leaf`, `tree_id`), and each creator's `address`/`share`/`verified`. Genuinely optional DAS companions (delegate, `non_transferable`, royalty and raw leaf fields, `collection_hash`, `asset_data_hash`, `flags`, content) still parse leniently.

changesets.summary: Reject incorrect instruction discriminators and trailing bytes
changesets.details: Reject incorrect instruction discriminators and trailing bytes in the remaining legacy generated instruction data decoders and named parsers. Preserve their existing data classes, encoder APIs, and decoder size metadata. Add regression coverage for instruction classification, truncated input, and nonzero decoder offsets.

changesets.summary: URL-encode dynamic path segments in REST endpoints
changesets.details: Dynamic path segments in the REST endpoints (`projectId`, `webhookId`, `address`, `wallet`, `stakeAccount`) are now URL-encoded, so a value returned by a compromised API cannot reshape a subsequent request's path on the Helius host. Fixed paths and the API-key query parameter are unchanged.

changesets.summary: Require secure transport for Sender submissions
changesets.details: Reject plaintext regional Sender endpoints before submitting transactions or bundles. The HTTPS default retains automatic region routing. Regional HTTP requires an explicit `allowInsecureHttpForTesting` opt-in in non-release builds and is always rejected in release builds, including by the Sender URL helpers.

changesets.summary: Track `helius-labs/helius-sdk` `v3.3.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances from `v3.2.0` to `v3.3.0`. The upstream release adds two new API surfaces (the parsed-events REST API and the parsed-streams WebSocket client), expands the preconfirmation WebSocket API, and fixes three bugs whose Dart counterparts are already equivalent: the Dart REST client surfaces raw non-JSON error bodies verbatim, the controller-based WebSocket client ends awaiting iterators on connection loss instead of hanging, and `HeliusConfig` builds fixed per-cluster URLs so the doubled-query-separator bug cannot occur. No code the Dart port implements changed. The new API surfaces are tracked for follow-up ports; see `docs/agents/upstream-audit-solana_kit_helius-v3.3.0.md`.

changesets.summary: Track `helius-labs/helius-sdk` `v3.4.0`
changesets.details:
The reference pin advances from `v3.3.0` to `v3.4.0`, and the previously deferred v3 surfaces are ported:

- **Parsed Events REST API** — `helius.parsedEvents` exposes `parseTransactions`, `getTransactionHistory`, and the new `scan` endpoint, with typed requests/responses, manual pagination, program/instruction/mint match filters, and a mainnet-only guard.
- **Parsed Streams WebSocket client** — `helius.parsedStreams` subscribes to decoded transactions with program/instruction/account-role filters and `full`/`matched`/`raw` details, reconnects and resubscribes automatically, reports the last delivered slot, and exposes `describeProgram`.
- **Preconfirmation filters, slot events, and coverage** — `preconfSubscribe` accepts server-side filters and `{slots: true}`, slot bank lifecycle frames decode as `PreconfSlotNotification`, and `getPreConfCoverage` reads the HTTPS coverage endpoint. Each subscription now uses its own connection, matching the upstream design.
- **`kitRpc` and MEV Protect** — `HeliusClient.kitRpc` exposes a standard `solana_kit_rpc` client over the Helius transport, and `HeliusConfig.mevProtect` (plus per-call Sender overrides) appends `mev-protect=true`.
- **Broadcast expiry re-check** — `broadcastTransaction` now polls to landing with an expiry derived from the latest blockhash and chain height, performing one final status read after the expiry height before throwing.
- **`getTransactionsForAddress` filters** — the request models the full v3 filter surface, including `filters.tokenTransfer`, and responses parse the live `{data, paginationToken}` shape.
- **DAS fixes** — `getAllTokenAccountsByOwner` accepts both page shapes, and the DAS `HeliusAssetInterface` enum uses the corrected `LEGACY_NFT` wire value with `MplCoreGroup` and `MplBubblegumV2`.
- **Staking constants** — `stakingU64Max` and `lamportsPerSolBigInt` expose the upstream `BigInt` constants.

The changeset is minor because the new clients and request fields are additive, while `GetTransactionsForAddressRequest` moves from the inaccurate `before`/`until` fields to the upstream `paginationToken` and `filters` shape.

changesets.summary: Bound untrusted inbound transport payloads
changesets.details: Add configurable inbound limits of 16 MiB, 64 JSON container levels, and one million JSON tokens. HTTP responses stop streaming on overflow, including when Content-Length is absent or understated, and custom decoders receive only bounded JSON. WebSocket channels close with application code 4009 on message or paused-listener queue overflow; queues default to 128 messages and 16 MiB per listener. Local and remote wallet sessions bound binary and base64 frames before copying or decrypting, validate decrypted JSON before parsing, and release session keys when a rejected frame closes the session.

changesets.summary: Reject insecure HTTP Jupiter endpoints in release builds
changesets.details: `JupiterConfig`'s `allowInsecureHttp` flag worked in release builds, unlike the core HTTP and WebSocket transports, which reject `http://` in product mode regardless of the flag — so a development-only flag could ship and send the `x-api-key` header and swap traffic in cleartext. The flag is now ignored in release (product) builds and `https://` is always required, matching the core transports and the documented security posture.

changesets.summary: Zero expanded-key intermediates after key generation and signing
changesets.details: `KeyPair.dispose` zeroes the stored seed, but `generateKeyPair`, `signBytes`, and `getPublicKeyFromPrivateKey` each derived a fresh 64-byte expanded key — seed plus public key — and left it unzeroed on the heap until garbage collection. All three now zero the expanded key (and the seed copy) in a `finally` block, so the only surviving copy of key material lives in objects whose lifetime the caller controls.

changesets.summary: Reject zero-byte item codecs with sentinel and remainder strategies
changesets.details: Ports the fix from `@solana/codecs-data-structures` v8.5.0 (#2089): constructing an `array`, `set`, or `map` codec whose item codec has a fixed size of zero with the sentinel or remainder size strategy now throws `codecsUnexpectedZeroFixedSizeItemForArrayLikeSizeStrategy` at construction time, on both the encoder and the decoder. A zero-byte item can never advance past a sentinel boundary or toward the end of the byte array, so decoding such a combination previously pushed elements until memory ran out. Zero-byte item codecs remain allowed when the collection size is explicit. The runtime zero-progress loop guards added in earlier port work remain as defense in depth.

changesets.summary: Accept odd-length strings in the base16 encoder
changesets.details: Ports the fix from `@solana/codecs-strings` v8.5.0 (#2117): `getBase16Encoder` no longer drops the last digit of odd-length strings. A trailing lone hex digit is encoded as the low nibble of a final byte — `'abc'` now encodes to `[0xab, 0x0c]` instead of throwing, matching the size `getSizeFromValue` reports. The single-character case is unchanged.

changesets.summary: Track `@solana/kit` v8.5.0
changesets.details: The reference pin moves from `anza-xyz/kit` v8.4.0 to v8.5.0, and the `@solana/kit` compatibility claim in `versions.json` and the root readme advances accordingly. See the audit in `docs/agents/upstream-audit-solana_kit-v8.5.0.md` for the full change map.

changesets.summary: Track `@solana/errors` v8.5.0: five new error codes
changesets.details:
Ports the error codes added upstream in `@solana/kit` v8.5.0:

- `keysVerificationRequiresExtractablePublicKey(3704007)` — WebCrypto-specific upstream; reserved here with its upstream number (the Dart verifier's public keys are always readable), with no throw site today.
- `codecsUnexpectedZeroFixedSizeItemForArrayLikeSizeStrategy(8078030)` — thrown by the array/set/map codecs when a zero-byte fixed-size item codec is combined with the sentinel or remainder size strategy.
- `walletInvalidMessageSignature(8900004)`, `walletInvalidSignInOutput(8900005)`, `walletInvalidNumberOfOutputs(8900006)` — wallet-account signer surface codes; reserved with their upstream numbers (that surface is not implemented in the Dart port yet).

Each code keeps its upstream `SolanaErrorCode` number so error codes remain interoperable across implementations.

changesets.summary: Allow binary fixed-points whose fractionalBits exceed totalBits
changesets.details: Ports the change from `@solana/fixed-points` v8.5.0 (#2102): binary fixed-point shapes where `fractionalBits` exceeds `totalBits` are now valid — e.g. an unsigned 8-bit value with 12 fractional bits represents values in `[0, 1/16)` — consistently with decimal fixed-points whose `decimals` may already exceed their `totalBits`. Values whose raw form does not fit in `totalBits` bits still fail the existing range checks.

changesets.summary: Fix the `SlotHashes` and `RecentBlockhashes` sysvar length prefix
changesets.details: Ports the wire-format fix from `@solana/sysvars` v8.5.0 (#2116): the entry arrays of `SysvarSlotHashes` and `SysvarRecentBlockhashes` are prefixed with a `u64` length on chain, not a `u32` one. The codecs now use `u64`, so decoded slots, hashes, and fee values are no longer shifted by four bytes.

changesets.summary: Reject sentinels found across the encoded-bytes/sentinel boundary
changesets.details: Ports the encoder hardening from `@solana/codecs-core` v8.6.0: `addCodecSentinel` now checks for the sentinel within the concatenation of the encoded bytes and the appended sentinel, so a value ending with the sentinel's own prefix (e.g. encoded bytes ending `6c` with sentinel `6c6c`) is rejected — the decoder would otherwise stop at that straddling occurrence instead of the real sentinel.

changesets.summary: Track `@solana/kit` v8.6.0
changesets.details: The reference pin moves from `anza-xyz/kit` v8.5.0 to v8.6.0, and the `@solana/kit` compatibility claim in `versions.json` and the root readme advances accordingly. See the audit in `docs/agents/upstream-audit-solana_kit-v8.6.0.md` for the full change map.

changesets.summary: Track `@solana/errors` v8.6.0: one new error code
changesets.details: Adds `walletFeatureVersionUnsupported` (8900007) with its upstream number and message: the wallet supports an older version of a requested feature than required. Reserved with no throw site today — the wallet-account feature-negotiation surface is not implemented in the Dart port yet.

changesets.summary: Make channel pool entry destruction idempotent
changesets.details: Ports #2121 from `@solana/rpc-subscriptions` v8.6.0: destroying a pool entry that is already gone now returns early. Previously, when the last subscriber of a channel that had already errored or failed to construct aborted, the destroy path could remove an unrelated, healthy channel that still had its own subscribers.

changesets.summary: Decode the v1 transaction config from `json` RPC responses
changesets.details: Ports #2132 from `@solana/transaction-introspection` v8.6.0: `decodeTransactionFromRpcResponse` now reads `message.transactionConfig` from a version 1 `'json'`-encoded response and fills the compiled message's `configMask` and `configValues`, matching what the `base64` and `base58` decoders already produced. Previously the synthesized v1 message always reported an empty config.

changesets.summary: Export `decompileTransactionConfig`
changesets.details: Ports #2134 from `@solana/transaction-messages` v8.6.0: `decompileTransactionConfig(configMask, configValues)` decodes the compiled config of a version 1 transaction message into a `V1TransactionConfig` without decompiling the whole message. The decompiler now delegates to it, preserving existing empty-config-to-null semantics. Config values that are missing, unexpected, or of the wrong kind still throw as before.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/loader-v3` `js@v0.8.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.8.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/memo` `js@v0.16.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.16.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Track `@solana-mobile/mobile-wallet-adapter-protocol-kit` `3.0.1`
changesets.details: The reference pin shared by the Mobile Wallet Adapter packages advances to `protocol-kit@3.0.1`. The upstream release is a JavaScript module-organization refactor — `startRemoteScenario` moves into its own module so React Native builds can exclude it — plus example-app and dev dependency bumps. The function body is unchanged from 3.0.0 and the Dart port has no module-graph or React Native fork concept, so no Dart code changes; the released patch carries the pin advance and the re-rendered support tables. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-solana_kit_mobile_wallet_adapter-v3.0.1.md`.

changesets.summary: Validate the complete intent of portal publication transactions
changesets.details:
Require complete local intent validation before signing portal transactions. Release minting now checks the exact CreateV1/MintV1 sequence, metadata name and URI, token recipient, supply, authorities, account privileges and derived addresses. Collection verification checks the exact Verify(CollectionV1) instruction. Reject extra or altered instructions, lookup tables, v1 messages and excessive priority fees.

`ReleaseMintValidation` now requires `expectedName` and `expectedMetadataUri`. Calling `signPreparedTransaction` without validation throws before signing. Only the documented publication instruction templates are accepted.

```dart
ReleaseMintValidation(
  expectedBlockhash: prepared.blockhash,
  expectedFeePayerAddress: payerAddress,
  expectedSignerAddress: publisherAddress,
  expectedMintAddress: prepared.mintAddress,
  expectedAppMintAddress: appMintAddress,
  expectedName: releaseName,
  expectedMetadataUri: releaseMetadataUri,
);
```

changesets.summary: Remove the sendBufferHighWatermark no-op option
changesets.details: `WebSocketChannelConfig.sendBufferHighWatermark` and the matching `DefaultRpcSubscriptionsChannelConfig.sendBufferHighWatermark` were documented as send-buffer high watermarks that queue outbound messages client-side once exceeded. No such behavior existed: `send` always handed each message straight to the WebSocket, because `web_socket_channel` exposes no buffered-amount state or drain signal to enforce it against. Both options are removed; outbound traffic is limited to small client-generated subscribe and unsubscribe frames, so no bound is needed. Code that set the option should simply drop the argument.

changesets.summary: Repair corrupted README documentation sections
changesets.details: Five package READMEs carried a mangled documentation region: a duplicated Installation section with an unfilled `^` version placeholder, a stray `:::` container marker, and an orphaned `packageDocumentationSection` closing tag with no opening tag. The sections now match the mdt consumer-block structure the rest of the workspace uses, so `mdt check` passes with validators that flag unmatched tags (mdt 0.9.6+) and the published READMEs no longer show two conflicting Installation sections.

changesets.summary: Bind native SIWS proofs to the requested challenge
changesets.details: Reject mobile Sign In With Solana proofs unless the signed bytes match the canonical message for the requested challenge and authorized account. This binds the nonce, origin, requested address, timestamps, request ID, and ordered resources, preventing valid signatures over stale or unrelated messages from satisfying a new request. Preserve trailing whitespace in SIWS field values so canonical serialization cannot collapse distinct challenges.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/stake` `js@v0.11.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.11.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json` (the one IDL delta is the program version string, proven output-neutral by generating the Dart package at both pins), so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Implement the space argument of stringifyJsonWithBigInts
changesets.details: `stringifyJsonWithBigInts` accepted a `space` parameter named after `JSON.stringify`'s but silently ignored it, so callers asking for pretty-printed output always got compact JSON with no error. The parameter now works exactly like its upstream counterpart: an int indents by that many spaces (clamped to ten, zero or negative stays compact) and a string is repeated at each nesting level (first ten characters), with `": "` separators and the same newline placement as `JSON.stringify`. Compact output — the default used by the RPC transports — is byte-for-byte unchanged.

changesets.summary: Pass the fork datasource URL through the environment
changesets.details: `Surfnet` passed a fork's upstream RPC URL — whose query string commonly carries an API key — as a `--rpc-url` process argument, where it was world-readable through `ps` and `/proc` on the machine running Surfnet. The URL now rides in the `SURFPOOL_DATASOURCE_RPC_URL` environment variable, which the CLI supports natively; output redaction is unchanged.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/system` `js@v0.16.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.16.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/token-2022` `js@v0.20.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.20.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Track `solana-program/token` `js@v0.18.0`
changesets.details: The reference pin advances to `js@v0.18.0`. The upstream release regenerates the TypeScript client without changing the program's `idl.json`, so no generated Dart code changes. See `docs/agents/upstream-audit-program-pins-2026-10-16.md`.

changesets.summary: Guard transaction encoding and decoding against empty and truncated bytes
changesets.details:
Three upstream error codes were defined but never thrown, and the paths they describe failed with less useful errors:

- Encoding a transaction with empty message bytes produced a signatures-first wire envelope of a zero-length message; it now throws `transactionCannotEncodeWithEmptyMessageBytes`.
- Decoding an empty byte array failed inside the shortU16 codec; it now throws `transactionCannotDecodeEmptyTransactionBytes`.
- A signature count larger than the remaining bytes can hold failed inside the signature reader with a range error; it now throws `transactionSignatureCountTooHighForTransactionBytes` with the expected count and byte length in the context.

changesets.summary: Correct the release-mode lockdown wording in transport docs
changesets.details: The HTTP transport's insecure-scheme guard uses `dart.vm.product`, which is true in release builds but not in Flutter profile builds; the code comment claimed "release/profile mode". The comment (and the matching WebSocket one) now says release (product) builds, matching the enforced behavior and `SECURITY.md`.

changesets.summary: Use trusted system permissions during key export
changesets.details: Use an absolute system path for chmod during key pair export so an inherited PATH cannot substitute an executable. Preserve private staging directory and key file permissions.

changesets.summary: Refresh generated upstream version tables and align validation tests
changesets.details: Regenerate the upstream version tables embedded in the generated program-client READMEs after the 2026-10-12 release (docs-only, produced by `docs:update`), and update two validation tests to the address-scoped error code now thrown for non-base58 strings: `assertIsBlockhash` and the RPC transaction decoder's loaded-address checks expect `addressesInvalidBase58EncodedAddress` instead of the codec-internal error that used to leak through.

changesets.summary: Verify direct mobile wallet signing results
changesets.details: Verify direct `KitMobileWallet` signing responses before returning them. Reject incorrect output counts, changed transaction or message bytes, forged signatures, altered existing cosignatures, and sign-in proofs that do not match the authorized account and requested SIWS fields. Validate reported transaction IDs against the submitted message and fee payer. Signing now requires authorization or reauthorization through the same wrapper, and pending responses are rejected if authorization changes.

entries:
- **Throw the address-scoped error for non-base58 address characters.** `assertIsAddress` validated string length and decoded byte count with dedicated `SolanaErrorCode`s, but a string in range whose characters fall outside the base58 alphabet leaked the codec's own error instead. That input now throws `SolanaErrorCode.addressesInvalidBase58EncodedAddress` with the `putativeAddress` context and the codec failure as its cause, matching the upstream `@solana/kit` error contract. `isAddress` still returns false for the same input.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_address_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

- **Validate Anchor IDL discriminators.** Reject missing, empty, non-integer, and out-of-range instruction, account, and event discriminators during IDL parsing. Preserve valid custom lengths and make parsed discriminator bytes immutable. Prevent empty discriminators from matching instruction, account, or event payloads, including when IDL entries are constructed manually.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_anchor_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [0f54cb7](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/0f54cb7e7e71e965fb43764cb7a9dafefd7400da)

#### Require Anchor IDL names and error codes, and attribute encode failures

_Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_anchor_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

`parseAnchorIdl` silently turned an IDL instruction, error, or defined type with a missing name into the empty string — every such node then collided under the `''` key in the instruction, error, and type maps — and an error entry without a numeric `code` became code zero, silently mis-keying program error decoding. Both now throw `ArgumentError` naming the offending entry.

`AnchorCoder`'s encode helpers no longer drop the field context they are given: a value that fails to encode inside an instruction argument or account field now surfaces as an `ArgumentError` naming that field instead of a bare codec error.

- **Reject cyclic Anchor IDL type dependencies.** Reject cyclic Anchor IDL type dependencies with an `ArgumentError` during codec construction instead of exhausting the call stack. Apply the check to direct codec requests, instructions, accounts, and events while preserving repeated acyclic references.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_anchor_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [640aee8](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/640aee875464cf9fb1b30e981fd35d923b447e7a)

- **Repair corrupted README documentation sections.** Five package READMEs carried a mangled documentation region: a duplicated Installation section with an unfilled `^` version placeholder, a stray `:::` container marker, and an orphaned `packageDocumentationSection` closing tag with no opening tag. The sections now match the mdt consumer-block structure the rest of the workspace uses, so `mdt check` passes with validators that flag unmatched tags (mdt 0.9.6+) and the published READMEs no longer show two conflicting Installation sections.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_anchor_, 🟢 _solana_kit_jupiter_, 🟢 _solana_kit_mpl_core_, 🟢 _solana_kit_mpl_token_metadata_, 🟢 _solana_kit_squads_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

- **Reject sentinels found across the encoded-bytes/sentinel boundary.** Ports the encoder hardening from `@solana/codecs-core` v8.6.0: `addCodecSentinel` now checks for the sentinel within the concatenation of the encoded bytes and the appended sentinel, so a value ending with the sentinel's own prefix (e.g. encoded bytes ending `6c` with sentinel `6c6c`) is rejected — the decoder would otherwise stop at that straddling occurrence instead of the real sentinel.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_codecs_core_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e3d08a9](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/e3d08a9ef215e7d2fe6b53943b851925bbbfb2ac)

- **Reject zero-byte item codecs with sentinel and remainder strategies.** Ports the fix from `@solana/codecs-data-structures` v8.5.0 (#2089): constructing an `array`, `set`, or `map` codec whose item codec has a fixed size of zero with the sentinel or remainder size strategy now throws `codecsUnexpectedZeroFixedSizeItemForArrayLikeSizeStrategy` at construction time, on both the encoder and the decoder.   _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_codecs_data_structures_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)

A trailing lone hex digit is encoded as the low nibble of a final byte — `'abc'` now encodes to `[0xab, 0x0c]` instead of throwing, matching the size `getSizeFromValue` reports. The single-character case is unchanged.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_codecs_strings_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)

  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_fixed_points_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f5511db](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/f5511db86d75f6d90aec21c99d1d4f397252c954)

No value the exponent path accepted before changes.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_spec_types_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)

- **Implement the space argument of stringifyJsonWithBigInts.** `stringifyJsonWithBigInts` accepted a `space` parameter named after `JSON.stringify`'s but silently ignored it, so callers asking for pretty-printed output always got compact JSON with no error. The parameter now works exactly like its upstream counterpart: an int indents by that many spaces (clamped to ten, zero or negative stays compact) and a string is repeated at each nesting level (first ten characters), with `": "` separators and the same newline placement as `JSON.stringify`. Compact output — the default used by the RPC transports — is byte-for-byte unchanged.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_spec_types_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

- **Make channel pool entry destruction idempotent.** Ports #2121 from `@solana/rpc-subscriptions` v8.6.0: destroying a pool entry that is already gone now returns early. Previously, when the last subscriber of a channel that had already errored or failed to construct aborted, the destroy path could remove an unrelated, healthy channel that still had its own subscribers.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_subscriptions_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e3d08a9](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/e3d08a9ef215e7d2fe6b53943b851925bbbfb2ac)

- **Correct the release-mode lockdown wording in transport docs.** The HTTP transport's insecure-scheme guard uses `dart.vm.product`, which is true in release builds but not in Flutter profile builds; the code comment claimed "release/profile mode". The comment (and the matching WebSocket one) now says release (product) builds, matching the enforced behavior and `SECURITY.md`.

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)

- **Refresh generated upstream version tables and align validation tests.** Regenerate the upstream version tables embedded in the generated program-client READMEs after the 2026-10-12 release (docs-only, produced by `docs:update`), and update two validation tests to the address-scoped error code now thrown for non-base58 strings: `assertIsBlockhash` and the RPC transaction decoder's loaded-address checks expect `addressesInvalidBase58EncodedAddress` instead of the codec-internal error that used to leak through.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_types_, 🟢 _solana_kit_transaction_introspection_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

#### Guard transaction encoding and decoding against empty and truncated bytes

_Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_transactions_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

Three upstream error codes were defined but never thrown, and the paths they describe failed with less useful errors:

- Encoding a transaction with empty message bytes produced a signatures-first wire envelope of a zero-length message; it now throws `transactionCannotEncodeWithEmptyMessageBytes`.
- Decoding an empty byte array failed inside the shortU16 codec; it now throws `transactionCannotDecodeEmptyTransactionBytes`.
- A signature count larger than the remaining bytes can hold failed inside the signature reader with a range error; it now throws `transactionSignatureCountTooHighForTransactionBytes` with the expected count and byte length in the context.

- **Reject zero-byte item codecs with sentinel and remainder strategies.** Ports the fix from `@solana/codecs-data-structures` v8.5.0 (#2089): constructing an `array`, `set`, or `map` codec whose item codec has a fixed size of zero with the sentinel or remainder size strategy now throws `codecsUnexpectedZeroFixedSizeItemForArrayLikeSizeStrategy` at construction time, on both the encoder and the decoder. A zero-byte item can never advance past a sentinel boundary or toward the end of the byte array, so decoding such a combination previously pushed elements until memory ran out. Zero-byte item codecs remain allowed when the collection size is explicit. The runtime zero-progress loop guards added in earlier port work remain as defense in depth.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_codecs_data_structures_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)
- **Accept odd-length strings in the base16 encoder.** Ports the fix from `@solana/codecs-strings` v8.5.0 (#2117): `getBase16Encoder` no longer drops the last digit of odd-length strings. A trailing lone hex digit is encoded as the low nibble of a final byte — `'abc'` now encodes to `[0xab, 0x0c]` instead of throwing, matching the size `getSizeFromValue` reports. The single-character case is unchanged.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_codecs_strings_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)
- **Allow binary fixed-points whose fractionalBits exceed totalBits.** Ports the change from `@solana/fixed-points` v8.5.0 (#2102): binary fixed-point shapes where `fractionalBits` exceeds `totalBits` are now valid — e.g. an unsigned 8-bit value with 12 fractional bits represents values in `[0, 1/16)` — consistently with decimal fixed-points whose `decimals` may already exceed their `totalBits`.   _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_fixed_points_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)
- **Reject insecure HTTP Jupiter endpoints in release builds.** `JupiterConfig`'s `allowInsecureHttp` flag worked in release builds, unlike the core HTTP and WebSocket transports, which reject `http://` in product mode regardless of the flag — so a development-only flag could ship and send the `x-api-key` header and swap traffic in cleartext.   _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)
- **Zero expanded-key intermediates after key generation and signing.** `KeyPair.dispose` zeroes the stored seed, but `generateKeyPair`, `signBytes`, and `getPublicKeyFromPrivateKey` each derived a fresh 64-byte expanded key — seed plus public key — and left it unzeroed on the heap until garbage collection.   _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_keys_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)
- **Use trusted system permissions during key export.** Use an absolute system path for chmod during key pair export so an inherited PATH cannot substitute an executable. Preserve private staging directory and key file permissions.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_keys_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f5511db](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/f5511db86d75f6d90aec21c99d1d4f397252c954)
- **Bound untrusted inbound transport payloads.** Add configurable inbound limits of 16 MiB, 64 JSON container levels, and one million JSON tokens. Local and remote wallet sessions bound binary and base64 frames before copying or decrypting, validate decrypted JSON before parsing, and release session keys when a rejected frame closes the session.

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f240282](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/f240282055735bd5694832f94d7d8f6a905d5960)
- **Bound BigInt materialization from plain integer literals.** `parseJsonWithBigInts` capped positive-exponent expansion at 10,000 but accepted a plain integer literal of any length, so a hostile RPC response containing a multi-megabyte integer forced a same-sized `BigInt` allocation for a cost far cheaper for the sender than for this process. Integer literals are now rejected when they would materialize more than 10,001 digits — the same ceiling the exponent cap already permits — on both the plain and the mantissa-plus-exponent paths. No value the exponent path accepted before changes.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_spec_types_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)
- **Implement the space argument of stringifyJsonWithBigInts.** `stringifyJsonWithBigInts` accepted a `space` parameter named after `JSON.stringify`'s but silently ignored it, so callers asking for pretty-printed output always got compact JSON with no error. The parameter now works exactly like its upstream counterpart: an int indents by that many spaces (clamped to ten, zero or negative stays compact) and a string is repeated at each nesting level (first ten characters), with `": "` separators and the same newline placement as `JSON.stringify`. Compact output — the default used by the RPC transports — is byte-for-byte unchanged.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_spec_types_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)
- **Make channel pool entry destruction idempotent.** Ports #2121 from `@solana/rpc-subscriptions` v8.6.0: destroying a pool entry that is already gone now returns early. Previously, when the last subscriber of a channel that had already errored or failed to construct aborted, the destroy path could remove an unrelated, healthy channel that still had its own subscribers.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_subscriptions_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e3d08a9](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/e3d08a9ef215e7d2fe6b53943b851925bbbfb2ac)
- **Correct the release-mode lockdown wording in transport docs.** The HTTP transport's insecure-scheme guard uses `dart.vm.product`, which is true in release builds but not in Flutter profile builds; the code comment claimed "release/profile mode". The comment (and the matching WebSocket one) now says release (product) builds, matching the enforced behavior and `SECURITY.md`.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_rpc_transport_http_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ad4d903](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/ad4d903443f06270c48a9ad135ad416147b020ae)

#### Guard transaction encoding and decoding against empty and truncated bytes

_Packages:_ 🟢 _solana_kit_transactions_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

entries:
- **Validate Anchor IDL discriminators.** Reject missing, empty, non-integer, and out-of-range instruction, account, and event discriminators during IDL parsing. Preserve valid custom lengths and make parsed discriminator bytes immutable. Prevent empty discriminators from matching instruction, account, or event payloads, including when IDL entries are constructed manually.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [0f54cb7](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/0f54cb7e7e71e965fb43764cb7a9dafefd7400da)

#### Bound fixed-array lengths from runtime schemas

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [43167d1](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/43167d1ed14951e6647f6f70d15a99a5890912d3)

Anchor IDL type parsing rejects negative, fractional, non-finite, and excessive fixed-array lengths. The upper bound is one million items, shared with array decoders through the new `defaultMaxArrayItems` constant.

Fixed-array decoders now enforce `maxItems` during construction, before byte-size calculations or element reads. This prevents hostile schema lengths from expanding zero-byte elements into unbounded lists. Callers can still choose a different decoder limit with `maxItems`; valid empty arrays and zero-byte elements remain supported.

#### Require Anchor IDL names and error codes, and attribute encode failures

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

`parseAnchorIdl` silently turned an IDL instruction, error, or defined type with a missing name into the empty string — every such node then collided under the `''` key in the instruction, error, and type maps — and an error entry without a numeric `code` became code zero, silently mis-keying program error decoding. Both now throw `ArgumentError` naming the offending entry.

`AnchorCoder`'s encode helpers no longer drop the field context they are given: a value that fails to encode inside an instruction argument or account field now surfaces as an `ArgumentError` naming that field instead of a bare codec error.

- **Reject cyclic Anchor IDL type dependencies.** Reject cyclic Anchor IDL type dependencies with an `ArgumentError` during codec construction instead of exhausting the call stack. Apply the check to direct codec requests, instructions, accounts, and events while preserving repeated acyclic references.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [640aee8](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/640aee875464cf9fb1b30e981fd35d923b447e7a)

- **Repair corrupted README documentation sections.** Five package READMEs carried a mangled documentation region: a duplicated Installation section with an unfilled `^` version placeholder, a stray `:::` container marker, and an orphaned `packageDocumentationSection` closing tag with no opening tag. The sections now match the mdt consumer-block structure the rest of the workspace uses, so `mdt check` passes with validators that flag unmatched tags (mdt 0.9.6+) and the published READMEs no longer show two conflicting Installation sections.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

#### Bound fixed-array lengths from runtime schemas

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [43167d1](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/43167d1ed14951e6647f6f70d15a99a5890912d3)

Anchor IDL type parsing rejects negative, fractional, non-finite, and excessive fixed-array lengths. The upper bound is one million items, shared with array decoders through the new `defaultMaxArrayItems` constant.

Fixed-array decoders now enforce `maxItems` during construction, before byte-size calculations or element reads. This prevents hostile schema lengths from expanding zero-byte elements into unbounded lists. Callers can still choose a different decoder limit with `maxItems`; valid empty arrays and zero-byte elements remain supported.

sections.title: Fixes
entries:
- **Reject zero-byte item codecs with sentinel and remainder strategies.** Ports the fix from `@solana/codecs-data-structures` v8.5.0 (#2089): constructing an `array`, `set`, or `map` codec whose item codec has a fixed size of zero with the sentinel or remainder size strategy now throws `codecsUnexpectedZeroFixedSizeItemForArrayLikeSizeStrategy` at construction time, on both the encoder and the decoder. A zero-byte item can never advance past a sentinel boundary or toward the end of the byte array, so decoding such a combination previously pushed elements until memory ran out. Zero-byte item codecs remain allowed when the collection size is explicit. The runtime zero-progress loop guards added in earlier port work remain as defense in depth.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)

entries:
#### Validate the complete intent of portal publication transactions

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [4459480](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/4459480176305b1d1f7cd4366f6e4f4d7f146add)

Require complete local intent validation before signing portal transactions. Release minting now checks the exact CreateV1/MintV1 sequence, metadata name and URI, token recipient, supply, authorities, account privileges and derived addresses. Collection verification checks the exact Verify(CollectionV1) instruction. Reject extra or altered instructions, lookup tables, v1 messages and excessive priority fees.

`ReleaseMintValidation` now requires `expectedName` and `expectedMetadataUri`. Calling `signPreparedTransaction` without validation throws before signing. Only the documented publication instruction templates are accepted.

```dart
ReleaseMintValidation(
  expectedBlockhash: prepared.blockhash,
  expectedFeePayerAddress: payerAddress,
  expectedSignerAddress: publisherAddress,
  expectedMintAddress: prepared.mintAddress,
  expectedAppMintAddress: appMintAddress,
  expectedName: releaseName,
  expectedMetadataUri: releaseMetadataUri,
);
```

entries:
- **Validate blockhash format before it reaches the wire.** The wire format stores a blockhash lifetime token as a fixed 32-byte value, but nothing validated the constraint's string: a blockhash whose base58 decoding was not exactly 32 bytes — for example one served by a compromised RPC — was silently truncated or zero-extended by the fixed-size encoder, producing a signed transaction whose lifetime token differs from the string shown to the caller. `setTransactionMessageLifetimeUsingBlockhash` now rejects such values with the new `SolanaErrorCode.transactionInvalidBlockhashFormat` (port-only code `5663043`), the blockhash counterpart of the existing `transactionInvalidNonceFormat` check.

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [253a913](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/253a9130ef81c0dd25e822fdcecebad7508a01cf)

Ports the error codes added upstream in `@solana/kit` v8.5.0:

- `codecsUnexpectedZeroFixedSizeItemForArrayLikeSizeStrategy(8078030)` — thrown by the array/set/map codecs when a zero-byte fixed-size item codec is combined with the sentinel or remainder size strategy.

Each code keeps its upstream `SolanaErrorCode` number so error codes remain interoperable across implementations.

- **Track `@solana/errors` v8.6.0: one new error code.** Adds `walletFeatureVersionUnsupported` (8900007) with its upstream number and message: the wallet supports an older version of a requested feature than required. Reserved with no throw site today — the wallet-account feature-negotiation surface is not implemented in the Dart port yet.

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [4c9341c](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/4c9341cd206b2a34f32e28398b771ae371505167)

The reference pin advances from `v3.3.0` to `v3.4.0`, and the previously deferred v3 surfaces are ported:

- **Parsed Events REST API** — `helius.parsedEvents` exposes `parseTransactions`, `getTransactionHistory`, and the new `scan` endpoint, with typed requests/responses, manual pagination, program/instruction/mint match filters, and a mainnet-only guard.
- **Parsed Streams WebSocket client** — `helius.parsedStreams` subscribes to decoded transactions with program/instruction/account-role filters and `full`/`matched`/`raw` details, reconnects and resubscribes automatically, reports the last delivered slot, and exposes `describeProgram`.

- **`kitRpc` and MEV Protect** — `HeliusClient.kitRpc` exposes a standard `solana_kit_rpc` client over the Helius transport, and `HeliusConfig.mevProtect` (plus per-call Sender overrides) appends `mev-protect=true`.

- **`getTransactionsForAddress` filters** — the request models the full v3 filter surface, including `filters.tokenTransfer`, and responses parse the live `{data, paginationToken}` shape.
- **DAS fixes** — `getAllTokenAccountsByOwner` accepts both page shapes, and the DAS `HeliusAssetInterface` enum uses the corrected `LEGACY_NFT` wire value with `MplCoreGroup` and `MplBubblegumV2`.
- **Staking constants** — `stakingU64Max` and `lamportsPerSolBigInt` expose the upstream `BigInt` constants.

The changeset is minor because the new clients and request fields are additive, while `GetTransactionsForAddressRequest` moves from the inaccurate `before`/`until` fields to the upstream `paginationToken` and `filters` shape.

sections.title: Fixes
entries:
#### Reject malformed Helius checkout responses instead of silently defaulting them

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

The hosted-checkout response models (`CheckoutInitializeResponse`, `CheckoutPreviewResponse`, `CheckoutStatusResponse`) parsed with `?? entries:
- **Validate blockhash format before it reaches the wire.** The wire format stores a blockhash lifetime token as a fixed 32-byte value, but nothing validated the constraint's string: a blockhash whose base58 decoding was not exactly 32 bytes — for example one served by a compromised RPC — was silently truncated or zero-extended by the fixed-size encoder, producing a signed transaction whose lifetime token differs from the string shown to the caller. `setTransactionMessageLifetimeUsingBlockhash` now rejects such values with the new `SolanaErrorCode.transactionInvalidBlockhashFormat` (port-only code `5663043`), the blockhash counterpart of the existing `transactionInvalidNonceFormat` check.

entries:
#### Guard transaction encoding and decoding against empty and truncated bytes

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [eedf4a4](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/eedf4a41807028ea4e43b01badd3b330013c7016)

Three upstream error codes were defined but never thrown, and the paths they describe failed with less useful errors:

- Encoding a transaction with empty message bytes produced a signatures-first wire envelope of a zero-length message; it now throws `transactionCannotEncodeWithEmptyMessageBytes`.
- Decoding an empty byte array failed inside the shortU16 codec; it now throws `transactionCannotDecodeEmptyTransactionBytes`.
- A signature count larger than the remaining bytes can hold failed inside the signature reader with a range error; it now throws `transactionSignatureCountTooHighForTransactionBytes` with the expected count and byte length in the context.

sections.title: Fixes
entries:
- **Verify browser wallet signing results.** Reject unverified browser wallet signing results. Check result counts, verify Ed25519 signatures, bind signed transactions and messages to their requests, validate every supplied sign-in challenge field and authorized account, and preserve offchain content and required signers. Copy request bytes before passing them to JavaScript so wallet providers cannot mutate the original request.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [1448d3f](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/1448d3f848348dec4e08b78e44c81fe1bafa05a1)

- **Bind native SIWS proofs to the requested challenge.** Reject mobile Sign In With Solana proofs unless the signed bytes match the canonical message for the requested challenge and authorized account. This binds the nonce, origin, requested address, timestamps, request ID, and ordered resources, preventing valid signatures over stale or unrelated messages from satisfying a new request. Preserve trailing whitespace in SIWS field values so canonical serialization cannot collapse distinct challenges.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [3d4f171](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/solana_kit/commit/3d4f171219d990605df88dfc9377d401a26c92a2)
